S1.rationale: The shipped Agent S3 Worker selects GUI actions from screenshots and task feedback. Independent upstream issue #235 shows the S3 CLI misreads arbitrary typed content containing done/fail/next/wait as a control signal. Current S3 CLI still substring-searches generated Python before executing it. This is an issue-backed product bug, not a defect first identified by Index.

S2.rationale: The ordinary shipped S3 mode is a single screenshot-to-GUI task loop with optional CodeAgent help rather than two competing viable S1 units. No current inter-worker coordination failure is required to fix the typed-text S1 action parser.

S3.rationale: Task step limits, pause/quit control and CodeAgent tool budget regulate one operative trajectory, not whole-current resource commitments across multiple S1 units. The S3 name in Agent S3 is an edition name, not VSM System 3.

S3*.rationale: Worker reflection and optional best-of-N rollout comparison provide task-time feedback or offline selection but do not establish a separately mandated independent runtime claim audit. The specific CLI control-word issue is not an S3* mechanism.

S4.rationale: Static procedural memory and current screenshot observations do not independently develop future organizational adaptations and adopt them into a later operating generation. No precise S4 product change is supported by this review.

S5.rationale: User task selection, provider and grounding configuration, local code permission and app pause/quit define operational constraints. They are not an identity-policy dispute and governing resolution loop; no S5 authority change has native demand.
